metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 ("a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)")

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Traffic video data and empirical traffic volumes from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, China, used to calibrate the SUMO simulation.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data is explicitly stated to be available upon request from the corresponding author; no public link or DOI is provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]... parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.description: Set up the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator for the Qingdao-Huangdao freeway merging area and calibrate driving behavior parameters using empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, tool named, all key parameters stated, but full driving behavior calibration details are omitted.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed... After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4 x 512 in pixels.
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle locations from raw video frames, apply zooming and down-sampling, and stack three consecutive frames to construct a 4x512 position matrix representing the traffic state.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, tools generic, parameters stated, but exact zooming ratio and down-sampling algorithm are not specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward rt after action at is defined by the following: rt = mu*vt + omega*qt, mu > 0, omega < 0
nodes_process.description: Define the reward function as a weighted sum of the average speed in the merging area and the average queue length at the on-ramp.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, mathematical formulation is exact, and all required weight parameters are explicitly provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Construct a deep Q-network with 3 CNN layers and 2 parallel FC output layers for multitask learning (predicting Q-value, speed, and queue length simultaneously).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, architecture fully detailed in Figure 7 with layer sizes, strides, and activations.

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update wi to minimize the loss function... The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames
nodes_process.description: Train the Q-network using the Adam optimizer, experience replay, target network freezing, and an epsilon-greedy strategy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, algorithm provided in pseudocode, and all hyperparameters are explicitly listed in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments... For comparative purposes, two scenarios are also considered... no control... and PI-ALINEA
nodes_process.description: Evaluate the trained DRL agent against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines over 20 simulation experiments. Measure travel times, speeds, queue lengths, and downstream volumes.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, evaluation protocol is clear, baseline parameters are provided, and multiple metrics are systematically reported.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data... the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: Divide the control area into 8 subareas and systematically remove information from each subarea to generate perturbed data, evaluating the impact on travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, procedure is described and parameters stated, but exact method of removing information (e.g., zeroing out vs masking) is not explicitly detailed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and hyperparameters are described, but code and exact data are not open, limiting full independent reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Vehicle travel times in the mainline over time (8:00 to 9:00) for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation setup in SUMO is well described, but relies on unavailable empirical data and closed code.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean travel times in 20 simulation experiments for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison based on 20 random seeds, but relies on unavailable empirical data and closed code.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed across distance and time for the three evaluated scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visualization of simulation outputs, but upstream simulation relies on closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length at the on-ramp over time for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visualization of simulation outputs, but upstream simulation relies on closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots showing the relationship between queue length and red ratio for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visualization of simulation outputs, but upstream simulation relies on closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Line plots showing queue length and occupancy over time for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visualization of simulation outputs, but upstream simulation relies on closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream volume over time for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visualization of simulation outputs, but upstream simulation relies on closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Box plot of travel time with perturbed input data, showing the effect of removing information from different subareas.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method is described, but relies on closed empirical data and code.
